sources.citation: Allen, J. H. and Greenough, J. B. (1903). Allen and Greenough's New Latin Grammar for Schools and Colleges. Boston: Ginn. Digital edition ed. M. Ayer, Dickinson College Commentaries, 2014.
sources.used_for: Standard reference grammar in English: forms, syntax, section numbers cited in lessons.
sources.access: Public domain; open online. Topic-to-page index in ag-index.tsv.

sources.citation: Bennett, C. E. (1918). New Latin Grammar. 3rd ed. Boston: Allyn and Bacon.
sources.used_for: Second reference grammar; paradigms in plain text for checking forms.

sources.citation: Gildersleeve, B. L. and Lodge, G. (1895). Gildersleeve's Latin Grammar. 3rd ed. London: Macmillan.
sources.used_for: Syntax in detail, with many cited examples.

sources.citation: Wiktionary, the free dictionary (English edition): Latin entries and inflection tables.
sources.used_for: Checking individual inflected forms, vowel lengths, meanings and etymologies (which cite de Vaan 2008).

sources.citation: Lewis, C. T. and Short, C. (1879). A Latin Dictionary. Oxford: Clarendon Press.
sources.used_for: Meanings, principal parts, usage with citations.

sources.citation: Francese, C. (2012). Latin Core Vocabulary. Dickinson College Commentaries.
sources.used_for: Frequency ranking used to choose which words to teach. Working copy in core-list.tsv (not shipped in the app).

sources.citation: Allen, W. S. (1978). Vox Latina: A Guide to the Pronunciation of Classical Latin. 2nd ed. Cambridge University Press.
sources.used_for: Authority for the restored pronunciation, syllable weight and stress.
sources.access: In copyright; consulted through recall and secondary summaries, so pronunciation claims are checked against ag1903 and wiktionary where they overlap.

sources.citation: Weiss, M. (2020). Outline of the Historical and Comparative Grammar of Latin. 2nd ed. Ann Arbor: Beech Stave Press.
sources.used_for: Authority for the history of sounds and forms (the why behind endings).
sources.access: In copyright; not openly online. Historical claims resting on it alone are labelled as from recall until checked against an open source.

sources.citation: Sihler, A. L. (1995). New Comparative Grammar of Greek and Latin. Oxford University Press.
sources.used_for: Second authority for historical explanations.

sources.citation: de Vaan, M. (2008). Etymological Dictionary of Latin and the other Italic Languages. Leiden: Brill.
sources.used_for: Etymologies of individual words, as reported in Wiktionary etymology sections.

sources.citation: Pinkster, H. (2015, 2021). The Oxford Latin Syntax. 2 vols. Oxford University Press.
sources.used_for: Modern description of syntax, word order and tense usage; corrective to schoolbook rules.

sources.citation: Devine, A. M. and Stephens, L. D. (2006). Latin Word Order: Structured Meaning and Information. Oxford University Press.
sources.used_for: Word order and its relation to emphasis.

sources.citation: Clackson, J. and Horrocks, G. (2007). The Blackwell History of the Latin Language. Oxford: Blackwell.
sources.used_for: History of the language from Early to Late Latin; background for parts 0 and 7.

sources.citation: The Latin Library (ed. W. L. Carey).
sources.used_for: Plain texts of classical and later authors, used to locate and check attested sentences.

sources.citation: Perseus Digital Library (Tufts University) and the Scaife Viewer.
sources.used_for: Texts with translations and parsing; second check on quoted passages.

sources.citation: Hammarström, H., Forkel, R., Haspelmath, M. and Bank, S. Glottolog: Latin (lati1261).
sources.used_for: Classification and reference list.

sources.citation: Dryer, M. S. and Haspelmath, M. (eds.) (2013). The World Atlas of Language Structures Online: Latin.
sources.used_for: Typological feature values for the Compare screen.

sources.citation: Corpus Inscriptionum Latinarum (1863– ). Berlin. Texts via the Epigraphik-Datenbank Clauss-Slaby.
sources.used_for: Inscriptions and graffiti, cited by volume and number.

sources.citation: Biblia Sacra iuxta Vulgatam versionem (Stuttgart Vulgate, ed. R. Weber and R. Gryson) and the Clementine Vulgate (1592).
sources.used_for: Late Latin reading passage.
sources.access: Text open online (e.g. The Latin Library).

sources.citation: Comrie, B., Haspelmath, M. and Bickel, B. (2015). The Leipzig Glossing Rules.
sources.used_for: Glossing conventions and abbreviations.
